evidence_summary: Effects Database explicitly catalogs a Nomad Tone Booster as Nomad (by UMI). Gearphoria's UMI history independently identifies UMI as a pedal maker founded by Richard Soloway in 1967 and says UMI made a Tone Booster that also existed under different brand names. This establishes a credible UMI relationship while the period Nomad-labeled primary evidence remains insufficient for public-grade promotion.

Richard Soloway's retrospective UMI history states that he first approached Gracin's Music in Freeport, New York with a lower-cost amplifier design and received an order for 100 units. This is strong evidence that Gracin's was an early UMI commercial customer, but it does not make Gracin's the builder of UMI pedals or prove the later Gracin's-branded fuzz was UMI-made.

The East Coast Fuzz literature identifies Gracin's as one of the New York/New Jersey marketed identities. UMI's documented early relationship with Gracin's does not establish that UMI built the Gracin's-branded fuzz, so the two records must remain separate until model-specific production evidence appears.

Tone Machines identifies the Nomad Banshee Fuzz as an Applied Audio product distributed by LIMMCO. This provides a direct counterexample to using the Nomad brand name as a factory proxy. Manufacturing dates remain uncertain, so chronology should remain open.

Tone Machines identifies the Nomad Rogue Fuzz as made by Applied Audio and distributed through LIMMCO. The Nomad branding therefore spans at least one UMI-linked Tone Booster and later Applied Audio fuzz products.
